compiled_state.title: Add _flock_write_json to ticket-lib.sh: cross-platform atomic JSON write primitive
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Testing Mode
UPDATE

## Story DD Coverage
This task is responsible for satisfying the following story done definitions:
- DD1: When this story is complete, the cross-platform locking approach for cycle-ledger.json is documented and references the existing plugin locking library (Python fcntl.flock wrapper), not the `flock` binary
- DD2: When this story is complete, the locking approach has been verified to work on macOS without Homebrew util-linux installed

## Implementation Steps
Add `_flock_write_json` function to `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh` immediately after `_flock_stage_commit` (around line 350).

### Function contract:
```
# _flock_write_json <lock_file> <staging_temp> <final_path>
# Cross-platform atomic JSON file write with exclusive lock.
# For use with non-git-tracked files (e.g., cycle-ledger.json in /tmp/).
# Unlike _flock_stage_commit, this function does NOT perform git operations.
#
# Args:
#   lock_file:     path to the lock file (created if absent; must be in a writable dir)
#   staging_temp:  absolute path to the staged temp file (same filesystem as final_path)
#   final_path:    absolute destination path (atomic rename target)
#
# Env:
#   FLOCK_STAGE_COMMIT_TIMEOUT  — lock timeout per attempt in seconds (default: 30)
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  — success: staging_temp atomically renamed to final_path
#   1  — lock timeout after max retries
#   3  — atomic rename failed (filesystem error)
#
# Cross-platform strategy (identical to _flock_stage_commit):
#   1. util-linux flock(1) binary if available and identified via --version
#   2. Homebrew util-linux at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/util-linux (macOS)
#   3. mkdir-based atomic lock fallback (works on any POSIX filesystem, including macOS without Homebrew)
_flock_write_json() { ... }
```

### Key implementation rules:
- Copy the `_flock_bin` detection logic verbatim from `_flock_stage_commit` (lines ~250-270 of ticket-lib.sh)
- Copy the retry loop (max_retries=2, flock_timeout from env) verbatim
- The only difference: replace the `git -C add && git -C commit` step with just `mv "$staging_temp" "$final_path"`
- Ensure lock file is created before acquisition: `: >> "$lock_file"` (as in `_flock_stage_commit`)
- On success: return 0 (lock released by subshell exit or rmdir in fallback path)
- On lock timeout: rm staging_temp, echo error to stderr, return 1
- On rename failure: rm staging_temp, echo error to stderr, return 3

### File: `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh`
Placement: after `_flock_stage_commit` function (approximately line 350), before `write_commit_event`.

### Justified-complexity note (Rule of Three):
`_flock_write_json` has one current caller (write-cycle-ledger.sh, Task 4 of this story). S2 (cycle-ledger schema task) and S4 (arbiter dispatch task) will add callers within this epic, reaching the three-caller threshold. The abstraction is in the canonical locking library (`ticket-lib.sh`) as required by the story's done definitions.

### macOS verification:
The mkdir fallback (tier 3) works without any external binary. On macOS without Homebrew util-linux:
- `command -v flock` may find a non-util-linux binary or nothing
- `_flock_bin` will be empty (after Homebrew check fails)
- mkdir fallback provides POSIX-atomic locking via `mkdir "$_lock_dir"` (atomic on NFS, HFS+, APFS)

Document this explicitly in the function header comment: "Works on macOS without Homebrew util-linux: falls through to mkdir-based atomic lock when util-linux flock is unavailable."

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Unit tests pass: `test_flock_write_json_atomic_write` passes in test-ticket-lib.sh
  Verify: bash $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/scripts/test-ticket-lib.sh 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -qE 'FAILED: 0'
- [ ] `_flock_write_json` is defined in ticket-lib.sh (as a sourced function, not a standalone script)
  Verify: bash -c 'source $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh 2>/dev/null; declare -f _flock_write_json' | grep -q '_flock_write_json'
- [ ] Function works when util-linux flock is absent (macOS-compat): atomic rename succeeds via mkdir fallback
  Verify: bash $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/tests/scripts/test-ticket-lib.sh 2>&1 | grep -v 'FAIL:'
- [ ] Lint passes (exit 0)
  Verify: LINT_CMD=$($(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.claude/scripts/dso read-config commands.lint) && [ -n "$LINT_CMD" ] && bash -c "$LINT_CMD" || true
- [ ] Format check passes (exit 0)
  Verify: FORMAT_CHECK_CMD=$($(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.claude/scripts/dso read-config commands.format_check) && [ -n "$FORMAT_CHECK_CMD" ] && bash -c "$FORMAT_CHECK_CMD" || true
- [ ] Function header comment explicitly states macOS-without-Homebrew compatibility
  Verify: grep -A5 '_flock_write_json()' $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh | grep -qi 'macos\|mkdir'

## Retry Budget
MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model)
On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages)
On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history
If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately
